title: Explore Numerical Expressions with Exponents
objective: I can write and evaluate numbers in exponent form using a base and a power.
model: repeated multiplication: expanded form b × b × … × b (n factors) beside the power b^n; squares and cubes as area and volume

widgets.component: Trailhead: area of a 9 cm square (81 cm², cm³ trap), 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2, 5 + 5 + 5 vs 5 × 5 × 5, factor count
widgets.root: Sets up repeated multiplication versus repeated addition; keys 81 cm², 32, Rafi, 5 recomputed and the cm³ distractor traps the unit confusion.

widgets.where: Practice §2 items 2.1-2.3, 2.5, 2.6 and §3 items 3.1-3.3 (mc, tbl, match, err)
widgets.component: Base Camp / Switchbacks: value of 4³ and 6², power as repeated multiplication, expansion tables, match powers to values, '5³ = 5 × 3' errors
widgets.root: Recomputed 64, 36, 5 × 5 × 5, table 9/16 and 64/64/125/10000, match 32/27/64/1000/25/128; the three err cards all target base × exponent, the lesson's central misconception. Table cells are numeric so '10,000' grades.

Needs grouping symbols and an exponent in one expression, and its hints/feedback teach 'parentheses first, then square, then multiply'; the order of operations with powers is the content of 6-4 (PEMDAS).
widgets.replacement: Replace with a single-concept power item: 'Evaluate 10³' (key 1000; distractors 30, 300, 10 000 named 'multiplied base by exponent', 'added a zero too few', 'added a zero too many') or 'Which is 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 written as a power?'. Hints: expand, then multiply two at a time.

widgets.component: Generated: base vs exponent, value of a power, power from repeated multiplication, doubling contexts, evaluate 3⁴ + 6³, greatest value, power of a given base
widgets.root: Checked 76 distinct draws per level: values exact (6³ = 216, 3⁴ + 6³ = 297), 'round 3' message-spread equals 3³ = 27, distractors are named slips (62, 12, 43).

widgets.component: How big is the file after 5 layers? / Why does the file grow so quickly?
widgets.root: Connect.check items 2-3 lifted without the scenario (a 4 MB track whose size doubles with each layer, 4 × 2ⁿ) or its 'File Size Doubles Each Layer' bar chart, so '5 layers' and 'the file' have no referent; 128 MB cannot be found.
widgets.replacement: Carry cfg.connect.scenario and cfg.connect.diagram into mastery items, or rewrite: 5.2 'A studio track is 4 MB and every added layer doubles the file size. How big is the file after 5 layers?' (key 128 MB, distractor 40 MB = 4 × 5 × 2) with the bar chart; 5.3 'Each added layer doubles the file instead of adding the same amount. Why does it grow so quickly?'.

widgets.component: Doubling stories, powers of 10, evaluate sums of powers, greatest value
widgets.root: Same generator as practice at higher difficulty; sampled answers exact.

widgets.component: Find the missing base (?² = 256, ?⁵ = 243) or missing exponent (6^? = 216), 'how many rounds to reach 128'
widgets.root: Asks for roots and logarithms (inverse of powering); the objective is to write and evaluate powers, and 'find the missing base' of ?² = 256 is only solvable by recalling 16² or taking a square root (Grade 8). Also prints '6^? = 216' with a caret.
widgets.replacement: Replace L4 with in-objective stretch: (a) 'Write 64 as a power of 2, of 4 and of 8' (select all three: 2⁶, 4³, 8²); (b) 'Which is greater, 2⁷ or 7²? by how much' (128 vs 49); (c) 'Fill in the exponent using the table of powers of 3' where 3, 9, 27, 81, 243 are printed and the unknown is drawn as a boxed superscript (3 then a box); delete all missing-base items.

widgets.component: Expedition Orders: 2³ = 6 error, 2⁵ routes at $3 each, doubling hiker table (8, 32, 256, 1024), 3⁵ vs 5³, cairn layers 2² + 3² + 4² + 5²
widgets.root: Recomputed $96, table values, 243 − 125 = 118, 54; each stem is self-contained.

widgets.component: Compare 2⁵ with 5², 2⁴ with 4², 3⁴ with 4³: type each value then which is greater
widgets.root: The 'Which is greater?' column must be typed as '2⁵', 'Equal' and '3⁴', graded by case-insensitive string equality on an input with inputmode=decimal; a student cannot type a superscript on that keypad, so a correct comparison is marked wrong.
widgets.replacement: Keep the four numeric columns (values 32, 25, 16, 16, 81, 64 grade by value). Replace the last column with a three-option control per row: [left expression] [Equal] [right expression] rendered as buttons, graded by index.

widgets.component: Sort powers below/above 100, match 12², 3⁵, 2⁹, 9³, tap the exponent on a 0-8 number line (3^? = 81)
widgets.root: Sort and match recomputed (64, 49, 81, 36 < 100; 100, 125, 128 ≥ 100). The number line is only a 9-tick picker, but the student must evaluate powers of 3 to choose, and tolerance is 0.

widgets.component: Trail Detective: 8² = 8 × 2, 2⁶ with base 6, 5⁴ = 5 + 5 + 5 + 5, '3⁴ is double 3²'
widgets.root: The four slips (multiply base by exponent, swap base/exponent, repeated addition, doubling the exponent doubles the value) are the lesson's misconceptions, each at the right step; 4.4 key 81 is nine times 9.

widgets.component: Summit Boss: same power as 5⁶, lamps on Day 10, not equal to 64, round-3 greeters, 2⁵ vs 5²
Write a power for shares after 6 hours and explain exponential growth; create your own
widgets.root: Passes on 40 characters and self-ticked rubric lines; the prompt also uses 'exponential growth', a term outside this lesson's vocabulary.
widgets.replacement: Require the numeric value (2⁶ = 64) in a box graded by value and a choice among three one-line reasons ('each hour multiplies by 2', 'each hour adds 2', 'the exponent is large') before the model answer opens; rename the prompt to 'Explain why the doubling grows faster than adding 2 each hour'.
